outcome_statement: runBrowserGoal (the real, live, model-driven overlay engine) gains a fail-closed risk-authorization guardrail: a click on a real observed element labeled with a financially/consequentially risky action (buy/purchase/pay/checkout/delete/cancel subscription/etc.) is blocked unless the caller explicitly passes allowRiskyActions:true, mirroring the existing confirmContext guardrail's own pattern and philosophy.
pain: The real production overlay engine already drives live browser sessions autonomously with zero action-risk gating -- nothing stops a model-proposed click on a real purchase/delete/cancel button.
value: The overlay becomes safe to build the rest of the autonomous opportunity/commerce engine on top of -- Adam's own framing: 'the whole program sits on that, all of them do.'
success_metrics: A synthetic risky-labeled click is blocked by default (ok:false, reason startswith risky_action_requires_authorization:)
The same scenario with allowRiskyActions:true executes normally
A goal that never touches a risky-labeled element is unaffected (regression-proof against existing callers)
failure_metrics: A risky-labeled action executes without allowRiskyActions:true
An existing non-risky goal (DNS cutover, account signup, marketing publish) is newly blocked by this change
constraints: BuilderOS system path only -- no agent hand-build
Must not change runBrowserGoal's existing confirmContext guardrail behavior
unacceptable_result: A risky action executes without explicit authorization; an existing live caller (browser-agent/run, marketing-publisher, browser-signup-orchestrator) regresses
ownership: ARC emits machine twin; Builder executes; Adam owns founder usability verdict
priority_fit: BP_PRIORITY rank 25 -- foundational, ahead of any new commerce/opportunity-engine mission

point_model.A: Vision -- Adam provides FP in development stage
point_model.B: Chair locks handoff -- corridor protected; Adam done until Alpha
